name: Tidal Dockline Waterproof Work Pant
description: Full waterproof construction with sealed seams and a rubberized outer shell over an insulating liner. Cut wide through the thigh for full movement when hauling lines or working wet cargo platforms. Standard in navy or dark teal; most pairs end up salt-stained and faded along the lower legs.
functionality: Waterproof sealed seams, thermal liner, wide-cut freedom-of-movement build
what_it_says: You work on or near water, you've been doing it a while, and you'd rather be warm than look good.
story_hooks: Tidal pants are sold in bulk to port labor contractors — finding a pair with a contractor's stencil code on the back waistband can identify which company employed the wearer.
The wide-leg cut makes them popular with Tier 1 residents who need to conceal items below the knee without obvious bulk.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian cargo silhouette with a pronounced wide-leg cut through hip and thigh, tapering slightly at the ankle. Heavy, structured appearance suggesting durability over fashion. Weathered aesthetic typical of dock and maritime work.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through hip and thigh with ample room for layering and movement; slight taper at ankle; high waistband for secure wear during physical labor; allows unrestricted leg mobility
physical_description.primary_material: Rubberized synthetic outer shell (ballistic-grade waterproof weave) laminated over insulating fleece liner; sealed seam construction throughout
physical_description.texture: Outer surface has subtle ribbed pattern from rubberization; slight tackiness to touch preventing slippage when wet; interior fleece soft and brushed; visible salt crystallization along lower legs on worn pairs
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary navy or dark teal with characteristic salt-fade gradient (lighter at calf and shin from repeated saltwater exposure); rust-orange oxidation stains at hem and pocket edges
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty friction-fit waistband with reinforced magnetic snap; dual zippered fly with rubberized pulls; cargo pockets with friction closures to prevent water infiltration
distinctive_features: Sealed seam tape running along all major construction points
Reinforced double-layer panel at knees and seat for abrasion resistance
Integrated drain grommets at ankle and cargo pockets
Reflective piping along outer seams (safety standard)
Woven manufacturer's label with QR-code tracking at waistband
Evidence of heavy patching or repair on thighs typical of heavily-worn pairs
Salt bloom discoloration forming natural patterns across lower legs
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 (working class functional); accessible to dockworkers and maritime labor across multiple income brackets
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals maritime/dock worker, industrial laborer, or coastal trade sector employment; worn by unionized cargo handlers, ship maintenance crews, and GLMZ Great Lakes freight operators
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily weathered; salt-stained legs with visible fade gradient; minor tears patched with rubberized tape; scuffed knees; rust-colored mineral deposits; still functionally sealed
